observations: The page number «18» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. L01-L05 end chapter 23 (p. 17, JP2 0049). L06: the heading of chapter 24, in bold, centred, with «C 72v, O 130r» in the left margin. L24: the heading of chapter 25, in bold, centred; no folio stands beside it.

L07: «elgeib» is printed in roman type, where the text has it in italics elsewhere (L04, and on p. 17); transcribed as printed. L05: «Ptolomaei» is letter-spaced; L10 and L13 «artifa», the altitude (al-irtifāʿ), L17 «elmahwar», the pole (al-miḥwar), L21 «elmuhit», the circumference (al-muḥīṭ), in italics. L24: «elfelek elmustakim», the right sphere (al-falak al-mustaqīm).

L10-L16: the latitude of a place is ninety degrees less the meridian altitude of the sun at an equinox; at another time the declination of the sun is first taken from the meridian altitude when it is northern and added when it is southern. L17-L23: the latitude is equal to the altitude of the pole, which is the centre of the circle that a circumpolar star describes, found from its greatest and least altitudes.

N03: «in raz elhamel C. {i:suprascr.}», with a full stop after the siglum before «suprascr.», where p. 16 has «C suprascr.» without it; the h of «elhamel» is printed with a thin arch. N12-N13: «sed verba … in rasura vel annulatione C habet» in italics, the words of C between them in roman.

The colons and semicolons of the text and of the apparatus stand after the thin space of the edition (8-12 px measured). Marks not transcribed: a speck in the right margin beside the last line of the notes.
